course_description:
Mechanical design principles. Design, manufacture and assembly of basic machine elements. Machine frames, welded, adhesive and bolted joints, fasteners. Stepped shafts and features, rolling element bearings; gear mechanics and manufacture. Design for strength, design for other mechanical failure modes including fatigue, stress concentration. Safety, ergonomics and standards.

This course introduces students to basic principles of mechanical design relevant to industrial practice. The contents include the design of specific machine components such as power transmission gearboxes containing gears, rotating shafts, keys and splines, bearings, seals, and gearboxes. Also included are: design of machine frames and assemblies including steel structures, fasteners and welded joints; considerations of safety and compliance with standards; assessment of mechanical failure (especially yielding, buckling, fracture and metal fatigue) in the context of machine design; fracture mechanics; and material properties most relevant to mechanical design; principles of sustainable design and social and environmental responsibilities of mechanical designers.

course_aims: MECH2100 develops students' capacity to design machine elements and mechanical assemblies for structural integrity. The course establishes a systematic framework for engineering design in which load path analysis, failure mode identification, material selection and design margin justification are treated as an integrated methodology rather than independent procedures. This framework is applied through three substantive engineering examples: gear transmission systems (including rotating shafts, bearings and mounting structures); threaded fasteners and bolted joints; and welded steel structures. Each example is used to develop and reinforce the skills of combined loading analysis, fatigue life estimation and design validation against relevant standards. On completing the course, students will be equipped to approach unfamiliar machine design problems systematically, decomposing them into tractable constituent problems and producing design solutions that are analytically justified, appropriately conservative and professionally documented.

learning_outcomes.description: Interpret design problems for machine elements within a structural integrity framework by tracing the flow of loads through structures and assemblies, and selecting appropriate methods for analysis.
Apply a connected taxonomy of failure modes (yield, fatigue, and fracture) to identify governing failure mechanisms for machine elements under realistic loading conditions
Explain how the mechanical properties of engineering materials govern the onset and progression of failure, and apply this knowledge to inform material selection for machine elements.
Select and justify design margins and safety factors with reference to uncertainty in loading and material data, consequence of failure, and the inspection and maintenance regime.

Design rotating shaft and gear transmission systems for structural integrity by applying gear design, combined loading analysis, fatigue life estimation, and bearing selection, using relevant standards and computer aided design tools.
Design bolted joints and threaded fasteners against failure by analysing preload, joint stiffness, fatigue and the influence of assembly practice on joint performance.

Assess the structural integrity of welded joints by analysing the effect of the fabrication process on material properties and stress concentration, and estimating the fatigue life using relevant standards.
Communicate design decisions for machine elements through systematic, evidence-based documentation.
Apply professional engineering practice including ethical, safety and environmental responsibilities.

learning_activities.topic: Lectures The lectures will cover fundamental theories of structural integrity and mechanical element design, and then apply this knowledge to the design of bolts, welds, gears, shafts, and related components. The designer's professional responsibilities will be emphasized. The lecture schedule and notes will be posted on Blackboard.
